esig_regulation.basis: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183. CAD art. 20(1-bis): an electronic document meets the written form and has the effect of c.c. art. 2702 when it bears a digital, other qualified or advanced electronic signature, or is formed by an AgID-compliant process after identifying its author. Art. 20(1-ter): use of a qualified or digital signature device is presumed attributable to its holder unless proven otherwise.

data_access_basis.basis: A private party needs a lawful basis under GDPR Art. 6(1), for example legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)); data on criminal offences needs official authority or a legal authorisation (Art. 10). A person can request their own data (Art. 15) within the Art. 12(3) period. D.lgs. 51/2018 implements Directive (EU) 2016/680 for competent authorities (art. 1).

timestamp_recognition.basis: Art. 41(1): a time stamp is not denied legal effect or admissibility solely because it is electronic or not qualified. Art. 41(2): a qualified time stamp is presumed accurate as to date and time and integrity of the bound data. Art. 42(1) sets the qualified requirements; Art. 24a(6) recognises qualified time stamps across Member States. CAD art. 20(1-bis): the date and time of formation of an electronic document are opposable to third parties if applied in accordance with the AgID Guidelines.

evidence_rules.basis: Outside the signature cases above, the suitability of an electronic document as written form and its probative value are freely assessed in court, considering its security, integrity and immutability.
The judge evaluates the evidence and states in the reasoning the results obtained and the criteria used.
Evidence acquired in breach of legal prohibitions cannot be used; this can be raised by the court of its own motion at any stage.

Writings and other documents representing facts, persons or things by photography, film, sound recording or any other means may be acquired. A copy may be acquired when the original is destroyed, lost or taken and cannot be recovered.
